title: Algebraic stacks admit 2-fibre products
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, morphisms and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Here an algebraic stack is a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas; smoothness is tested on scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be algebraic stacks over $S$ and let $a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $b:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be morphisms. The stack in groupoids $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$, whose objects over a scheme $T$ are triples $(x,y,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal A(T)$, $y\in\mathcal B(T)$ and $\alpha:a(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}b(y)$, is an algebraic stack. With its two projections and tautological 2-isomorphism it is a 2-fibre product in the 2-category of algebraic stacks over $S$.

source.place: Tag 04T2 (lemma-2-fibre-product); the stronger construction is Tag 04TF (lemma-2-fibre-product-general).

proof.text: Put $P=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$, using the triple construction. Its pullbacks and cartesian lifts are componentwise. A descent datum for triples consists of descent data for $x$ and $y$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:a(x_i)\simeq b(y_i)$. Descend $x_i,y_i$ in $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$; the sheaf condition for isomorphisms in $\mathcal C$ glues the $\alpha_i$ uniquely. Arrows of triples are pairs of arrows satisfying $b(v)\alpha=\alpha'a(u)$; their sheaf condition follows by gluing both components and checking this equality locally in $\mathcal C$. Thus $P$ is an etale stack.

source.place: Tag 04TF first paragraph; stacks.tex Tag 02ZL (lemma-2-product-stacks-in-groupoids); elementary componentwise descent in the etale convention

proof.text:
For any fibred groupoid $\mathcal D$ with representable diagonal and $x,x'\in\mathcal D(T)$, its isomorphism sheaf is an algebraic space: by the space-source representability lemma, $T\times_{\mathcal D}T$ is a space, and pulling it back along $T\to T\times_ST$ selects isomorphisms over the same test map to $T$. This pullback is a space by the space fibre-product lemma. Conversely, a scheme test $(x,x'):T\to P\times_SP$ of the diagonal has fibre the groupoid of $(z,z\simeq x,z\simeq x')$, equivalent to the discrete sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_P(x,x')$ by composing the second isomorphism with the inverse of the first. For $p=(x,y,\alpha)$ and $p'=(x',y',\alpha')$ the arrow equation gives
$$\operatorname{Isom}_P(p,p')=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal A}(x,x')\times_{\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal C}(a(x),b(y'))}\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal B}(y,y'),$$
with maps $u\mapsto\alpha'a(u)$ and $v\mapsto b(v)\alpha$. All three terms are spaces by the first calculation, so their fibre product is a space. This proves representability of $\Delta_P$.

Choose smooth surjective scheme atlases $U\to\mathcal A$ and $V\to\mathcal B$. The diagonal of $\mathcal C$ and the space-source representability lemma make $E=U\times_{\mathcal C}V$ an algebraic space. The natural map $E\to P$ factors as
$$U\times_{\mathcal C}V\longrightarrow U\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B\longrightarrow\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B.$$
The first arrow is the 2-base change of $V\to\mathcal B$ and the second that of $U\to\mathcal A$: eliminating the redundant identified object in either triple gives the indicated equivalences. The general fibred-groupoid calculus therefore makes $E\to P$ representable smooth surjective, without presupposing algebraicity of $P$ or of the intermediate category.

source.place: Tag 04TF final paragraph, through the composition of base changes

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to E$ from the definition of algebraic space. The general fibred-groupoid calculus identifies its space and discrete-groupoid properties, makes it smooth, and makes $W\to E\to P$ representable smooth surjective. Together with steps 1 and 2 this verifies all three defining conditions for an algebraic stack. All charts lie in the stipulated universes; no finite type or quasi-compact atlas is required.

For any algebraic stack $\mathcal H$, a morphism $\mathcal H\to P$ is precisely a pair $f:\mathcal H\to\mathcal A$, $g:\mathcal H\to\mathcal B$ and a natural isomorphism $af\simeq bg$: evaluate the morphism on each object to obtain its triple, or assemble those triples to construct it. A 2-morphism is precisely a pair of natural isomorphisms of $f,g$ satisfying the same compatibility equation as an arrow of triples. These constructions are mutually inverse and natural in $\mathcal H$. Since $P$ is algebraic by step 4 and morphisms and 2-morphisms of algebraic stacks are all those of their underlying stacks, this is the required 2-fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tag 04T2 final paragraph; explicit full-sub-2-category universal property

lean.statement: theorem algebraicStack_twoFiberProduct {S : Scheme.{u}} (A : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (B : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)) (C : BasedCategory.{v₃, w₃} (Over S)) (hA : IsAlgebraicModuliStack A) (hB : IsAlgebraicModuliStack B) (hC : IsAlgebraicModuliStack C) (a : BasedFunctor A C) (b : BasedFunctor B C) : IsAlgebraicModuliStack (moduliTwoFiberProduct a b) ∧ ∃ κ : (moduliTwoFiberFst a b).comp a ≅ (moduliTwoFiberSnd a b).comp b, (∀ z : (moduliTwoFiberProduct a b).obj, κ.hom.toNatTrans.app z = z.obj.hom) ∧ (∀ (H : BasedCategory.{v₄, w₄} (Over S)), IsAlgebraicModuliStack H → ∀ (p : BasedFunctor H A) (q : BasedFunctor H B) (e : p.comp a ≅ q.comp b), ∃ (l : BasedFunctor H (moduliTwoFiberProduct a b)) (α : l.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst a b) ≅ p) (β : l.comp (moduliTwoFiberSnd a b) ≅ q), ∀ x : H.obj, a.map (α.hom.toNatTrans.app x) ≫ e.hom.toNatTrans.app x = κ.hom.toNatTrans.app (l.obj x) ≫ b.map (β.hom.toNatTrans.app x)) ∧ (∀ (H : BasedCategory.{v₄, w₄} (Over S)), IsAlgebraicModuliStack H → ∀ (l m : BasedFunctor H (moduliTwoFiberProduct a b)) (α : l.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst a b) ≅ m.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst a b)) (β : l.comp (moduliTwoFiberSnd a b) ≅ m.comp (moduliTwoFiberSnd a b)), (∀ x : H.obj, a.map (α.hom.toNatTrans.app x) ≫ κ.hom.toNatTrans.app (m.obj x) = κ.hom.toNatTrans.app (l.obj x) ≫ b.map (β.hom.toNatTrans.app x)) → ∃! θ : l ≅ m, BasedCategory.whiskerRight θ.hom (moduliTwoFiberFst a b) = α.hom ∧ BasedCategory.whiskerRight θ.hom (moduliTwoFiberSnd a b) = β.hom)
